title: stagecraft
notGreen: 9 skipped (strict): an acceptance run runs every check

results.goal: a checkpoint's background effect switches the ST background deterministically, and re-applies on hydrate

the WI curator proposes a change off-path from real canon, the author reviews it on the drawer's cards (editing it when it is a text change), and the boundary write — whatever op kind the model chose — reaches the server file and the next generation's prompt
every curator action is journaled, it can never write the blackboard or a memory tier, and a write outside the story's allowlist is refused

results.prompt: Did the presentation (scene, background, cast) feel handled for you, without you asking?
results.anchors: 1 = nothing happened · 3 = noticed it once · 5 = the stage kept up with the story

results.goal: warden auto: a scripted reply that contradicts a seeded fact locked as canon produces one continuity note, and the claim the read takes from it is held in the reconciliation queue, never a live fact the warden enforces (v2.4 plan 07 contradiction fix); the next loud generation's prompt carries it, the one after does not. Under a journey judge mode (v2.4 plan 07) the check leaves the judge settings to the mode: --judge-uses warden --warden-mode auto is the on arm, and --judge-uses off is the control arm, where the same turns must make no warden call and no note may reach a prompt
warden review: the note waits for the author; a newer reply commits first, the note lapses, and no note reaches any prompt
both judge curators off (warden off, curator focus off): a contradicting reply and a generation make no warden or curator-filter call, add no proposal and put no note in the prompt

agency check auto (v2.4 plan 07 T22): a scripted reply that writes the player's act and words produces one agency note on the warden path; the next loud generation's prompt carries it, the one after does not, and the over-steer probe records reply N+1 (family agency). Under a journey judge mode: --judge-uses agencyCheck --warden-mode auto is the on arm; --judge-uses off is the control arm, where the same turns make no warden call and no Agency: line reaches a prompt
agency check review (v2.4 plan 07 T22): the agency note waits for the author; a newer reply commits first, the note lapses, and no Agency: line reaches any prompt

house rules auto (v2.4 plan 07 T23): a story with authored house_rules and a reply that breaks one produces a house-rule note naming the rule verbatim, and the captured GENERATE_AFTER_DATA prompt of the next loud generation carries it; the one after does not. Under a journey judge mode: --judge-uses houseRules --warden-mode auto is the on arm; off is the control

every warden family off (continuity warden off, agencyCheck off, houseRules off, judge on): a reply that writes the player and breaks a house rule makes no warden call, adds no proposal and puts no note in any prompt

reply.speaker: Ponticius
reply.text:
"Alright, you're going-a-to have to do better than that," *he says, his voice raspy, leaning over a wooden desk cluttered with maps and crumpled quest reports. He taps a calloused finger on a particularly weathered parchment.* "Smugglers on the docks? Dangerous business, but nothing we can't handle. You’re a seasoned adventurer, Max—I’ve got respect for that, but you can't just 'keep your head down' while the town’s bleeding coin and reputation."
*He straightens up, his graying beard catching the light from the flickering oil lamp.* "This ain't about playing it safe. It's about getting what needs to be done, and I've seen enough of you lot run into the dirt for lack of conviction. Those smugglers are moving goods through Xentar's waters—stolen property, maybe even undead artifacts from the Lich Queen's time that shouldn't be disturbed. You go in there quiet, and you get out with the damage done."
*Ponticius rounds the desk, his heavy boots thudding on the floor.* "So here's the way it is—you're taking that ferry, you're getting on the ship. You'll find the smugglers where you've run out of patience, and you'll make them talk or make them silent. Either you're coming back with information on who's running this operation, or you're not coming back at all." *His eyes harden, but there's a faint glimmer of something warmer there—a soft spot for those willing to take the risk.* "Now, are you going-a to stand there and wait or are you-a to do something about it?"

You're-a going-a-to find them, and you-re-a going-a to make them-a make-a them talk or make-a them silent."
*He pauses, his eyes scanning the dock's chaotic aftermath as the ferry begins to push off.* "Just-a remember—you're-a not alone on this boat. There's others. civilians and-a civilians who know-a too much. So be-a careful where-a you aim-a your-a skills."
*Ponticius leans against the railing as the ferry starts to move away from the dock, his gaze fixed on the dock where the smugglers had been. He watches as the boat cuts through the choppy waters of the bay.* "The ferry's-a going to a different dock, but the smugglers' hideout is-a nearby. You-'ll have-a to find it from the ferry's-a landing. It-a is-a flooded, but that-a won't matter to you,-a right?"
*His voice carries over the engine's rumble as the ferry's-a boat begins to pull away from the dock.* "Don't-a be-a thinking-a of-a returning without-a something-a, Max. The Guild is-a counting on-a you."
*The ferry's engine hums as it pulls away from the dock, leaving the dock and its choppy waters behind. Ponticius stays on the ferry for a moment, but his voice lingers in the air as the air grows colder and the damp air clings to theH-a ferry-a’s-a rail-a-a-a*
